The Potential $100 Trillion Market For Space Mining
One asteroid's worth of anything would crash the world's economy, would it not?

Mining these celestial objects would flood the market forcing them to be worthless. the only way they would be viable was for them to be used for massive space building projects like lunar stations or massive space stations. They would be economical but only if there was an asteroid size demand for them. I say we will mine for these materials, they will flood the market, they will drive costs waayyyyy down, and when they are at their cheepest, agencies will start building massive outer space projects.
Imagine all we needed for a post scarcity society was to mine a few asteroids? Then replicate what you want? Damn future, you're scary and bright
But the mining will likely be done by armies of unpaid robots owned by a few trillionaires living on Elysium.

No it would not, at least at the very beginning. I know that it is easy to think that once we mind shit ton of stuff and flood the market with that, the price of these materials will go down. Not, necessarily correct.

The price of anything is simply a dance between supply and demand. However there is always a base on how much price can go down, and that is production cost. There is two reasons why the price of these materials will go down significantly, once we start mining astroids:

  • The idea of the price go down because we will flood the market is sound, but we are missing an important point. Yes, when we mind shit ton, we are increasing the supply significantly. For the unit price to go down, the demand must stay at current levels. That will not happen. Our usage of rare metals is increasing rapidly, which is one of the biggest reason why those metals are becoming more expensive. Yes, with astroid mining, the supply will go up, but the demand is (has been) going up crazy amount, thus the unit price is not going to go that low.
  • As I mentioned, there is a limit on how much the price of a unit can go down, that is determined by production cost. If there is no profitability (selling goods for a price that is more than its cost), then no body in the right mind would invest into those businesses which aims to mind astroids. Initially, the cost of mining will be high, thus keeping the unit price at acceptable levels.
